pr_comments: Please review. I marked it as urgent. The gost engine will be committed immediately after this patch.
Not sure I like the ending `_legacy`. We have functions already that end with `_noconst`, could that be a suitable pattern to follow?
I don't have any preference here. The idea of the _legacy suffix is demonstration that the function works only for the legacy keys
I don't understand whether the test failures are relevant.
The test failures are of course relevant - the threadstest needs to be fixed to not use the get0() to test downgrading.
It needs to use the get0_RSA() instead.
Is the non-caching failure relevant? Everything else has passed.
I don't think it is relevant.
Merged. Many thanks for the thorough review!

issue_context.title: After merging the change constifying EVP_PKEY_get0 return value external gost test fails
issue_context.body:
The gost engine uses EVP_PKEY_get0*() functions and does not expect the return value being const. This makes the external tests build to fail.

A temporary workaround could be to make the gost engine build without -Werror. Otherwise this needs fixing in the gost-engine code.
comments: @beldmit Would you please look at this on the gost-engine side?
@t8m, will do.

Example of the failure:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/runs/2057812906
No, switching off the -Werror makes non-working build :(

Oh. It looks like we've got to the situation I tried to avoid as much as possible.

I'd suggest temporary switch off the gost tests until I deal with this stuff. I'm afraid there is no relevant API to replace it for the GOST engine.
It sounds real mysterious with a build that breaks when you remove `-Werror`...
The build doesn't, but the tests do

I am curious why this breaks. Shouldn't the Gost engine work with legacy keys only?

It should. I didn't investigate yet, but it may fall because of trying to modify the constant EVP_PKEY object

If the EVP_PKEY object has legacy origin it shouldn't be truly const. I.e., the key should be update-able although the get0 call returns it as const. If we broke that somehow, we need to fix that. @mattcaswell ?

Right...if legacy origin then it shouldn't be a problem.

I'm thinking we could even provide a new function EVP_PKEY_get0_legacy() that would return a non-const pointer but would return NULL if the key doesn't have legacy origin.

Or just use the get1 functions which are already non-const.
Or....actually maybe there isn't an EVP_PKEY_get1....'cos its void *...:-(

> Or just use the get1 functions which are already non-const.

It was the first idea but I didn't find it immediately

> Or just use the get1 functions which are already non-const.

Hmmm, except that functionality that's part of an EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD *must* be able to manipulate the internal legacy key, by design.  And that's exactly what an engine does.
Functions that are designed for EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD will have to unconst the return value of `EVP_PKEY_get0()`

An idea is to make `EVP_PKEY_get0()` return a non-const value, which the type specific counterparts (EVP_PKEY_get0_RSA() et al) return const values, with the argument that EVP_PKEY_get0() is more likely to be used from EVP_PKEY_METHOD and EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD functionality.
Yes, it's a great idea

Then we should also make it to return NULL if the key origin is not legacy.
